name: Spatial Layout → Social Affordances → Social Behavior

mechanism_chain.description: Spatial layout determines the density and type of social affordances: face-to-face seating, lingering zones, shared surfaces, visual connectivity. VGA connectivity predicts affordance cluster locations.

data.finding: Space syntax visual graph analysis (VGA) predicts locations of spontaneous social congregation with r ≈ 0.60-0.75
Face-to-face seating arrangements produce more conversation than side-by-side; shared surfaces (tables, counters) create social affordances

justification.backing: The spatial-to-social link is well-established in space syntax research. Visual connectivity and circulation patterns predict where people will stop, linger, and interact. Architectural configuration constitutes the affordance field that shapes social behavior distribution.
justification.qualifier: VGA predictions are strongest for movement and congregation; the specific social modes (conversation vs. observation) are less precisely predicted by connectivity alone.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if social behavior is determined primarily by social factors (who is present) rather than spatial factors (where affordances are located); but evidence shows spatial configuration has independent effect.

mechanism_chain.description: Affordance density modulates behavior: low density → solitary behavior dominates; moderate density → dyadic and small-group interaction; high density → social monitoring cost exceeds benefit (Dunbar saturation).

data.finding: Dunbar's sympathy group (~15 individuals) and conversation group (~4-6) represent cognitive limits on social tracking
Above ~6 simultaneous conversational groups in visual field, social monitoring cost exceeds benefit for most individuals

justification.backing: Dunbar's social brain work provides the cognitive constraint: humans can track ~15 individuals with emotional salience, ~4-6 in active conversation. Beyond these limits, additional social affordances produce monitoring cost without benefit. The architectural application is that moderate affordance density (supporting 3-5 social modes) optimizes the cost-benefit ratio.
justification.qualifier: The ~6 conversational groups threshold is a panel estimate, not a directly measured architectural quantity. Individual differences in social monitoring capacity are substantial.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupants selectively attend to a subset of available affordances, ignoring excess; but evidence suggests ambient social monitoring is not fully voluntary.

mechanism_chain.description: Optimal social affordance density supports occupant social needs without producing social exhaustion. Below optimum → isolation risk; above optimum → overstimulation.

data.finding: Social isolation biology activates below ~3 meaningful exchanges per day (see NM_SOCIAL_ISOLATION_ALLOSTATIC_001)
data.source: Cacioppo et al. (2006); Holt-Lunstad et al. (2010)

data.finding: Open-plan offices with excessive social density produce higher stress and lower performance than moderate-density designs
data.source: Brennan et al. (2002); office design literature

justification.backing: The bidirectional risk model: too few social affordances produces isolation biology (CTRA activation, IC2 drain); too many produces social exhaustion (mentalizing overload, vigilance cost). Optimal density minimizes total IC2 expenditure across both mechanisms.
justification.qualifier: The optimal density varies by population, task, and individual preference. No single architectural solution fits all contexts; the template identifies the trade-off structure rather than a universal value.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupants have complete control over social engagement (can withdraw at will); but architectural constraints often prevent optimal self-regulation.

sensorimotor_coupling.description: Number of distinct social modes simultaneously supported by a space

color_properties.description: Above this threshold, social monitoring cost exceeds benefit for most individuals. Based on Dunbar's sympathy group (~15 individuals ÷ ~2.5 per conversation group ≈ 6 groups).

key_references: Whyte, W. H. (1980). The Social Life of Small Urban Spaces. Project for Public Spaces.
Hillier, B. (1996). Space is the Machine. Cambridge University Press.

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — excess social affordance density produces chronic social monitoring cost (IC2 drain). Insufficient density fails to buffer isolation biology. Moderate density minimizes total IC2 expenditure.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — spaces that offer CHOICE of social mode (solitary nook alongside communal table) maximize AX4. Mono-mode spaces (all open or all private) constrain AX4.
